content_blocks.text: View PDF
A stakeholder is an individual or group who have an interest or concern in something e.g. an activity or a business.
When undertaking aprocurement exercise it is crucial you ensure that stakeholders are involved to:
provide their expertise and feedback
meet and manage their expectations
hold ongoing two way communications
gain their buy-in throughout all stages of the process
support the contract after it has been implemented
For procurement exercises, a User Intelligence Group (UIG) should be created. The UIG is a cross functional team containing key stakeholders.
The UIG will assist you with:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: developing the commodity/service strategy,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: the tender evaluation
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: the ongoing activities of contract/supplier management,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: monitoring,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: implementation,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: compliance and
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: benefits tracking
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: This group should have representation from key stakeholders within the participating Organisation(s). Members should include procurement and business/technical/customer representatives.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: The National Standards for Community Engagement principles may help when establishing the UIG. These principles are designed to support and inform the process of community engagement and improve outputs.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: All UIG’s should have a minimum of two members i.e. the Buyer and the end user.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Care and Support Services
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: All UIG’s (with the exception of Care and Support Services) should have a minimum of two members i.e. the Buyer and the end user
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Quickfire Guide
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: UIG Research
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: You should undertake appropriate research before the first UIG meeting. For example:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Gain an understanding of the commodity/service market from desktop research e.g. via the internet
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Speak to potential suppliers or industry representatives
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Meet with individual key stakeholders and end-users
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Review historical spend patterns, if appropriate
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Gather information from other public sector contacts, such as Centres of Expertise or peers
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Read previous tenders or commodity/service strategies
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: This research will help you gain an initial understanding of:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: the commodity/service,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: the Organisation's requirements,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: market conditions
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: risks, issues and barriers to success.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: any contracts you may be able to access without the cost, time and risk of developing your own contract.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: At this stage, consideration should also be given to the sustainable procurement factors to be built into your process. You can also identify any expert or informed input that will be required e.g. guidance from climate change experts on carbon in the specific supply chain, or input from Economic Development officers regarding employment opportunities.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholder Mapping
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: The benefits of establishing a UIG are:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: The ability to draw on the cross-functional expertise within the group
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholder views are considered in the decision making process
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Clear communication channels can be established
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Presents 'one face' to potential suppliers
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Formalises the governance arrangements and identifies the decision makers
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Clarifies roles and responsibilities
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Facilitates the generation of ideas
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Facilitates buy-in and compliance
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholders working together to understand and overcome any barriers to success
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Embed best practice
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Support the implementation of continuous improvement processes to safeguard the future of public service for future generations
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: bring together the ideas and insights of groups to obtain a holistic view.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholders should work to:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Encourage and sponsor continuous improvement
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Encourage innovation
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Understand and remove any potential barriers to success
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Where there are a large number of stakeholders, for example a collaborative contract, it may not be possible to have all stakeholders represented on the UIG.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholder mapping is a useful tool to help identify who should be represented. This is based upon their likely impact upon the success of the project.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: You must also ensure you understand your Organisation's policy or requirements regarding engaging with end users/customers of the commodity or service and whether they should also be involved in the UIG.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Depending on the specifics of the procurement exercise, the Buyer may ask stakeholders the following questions prior to the starting their procurement:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Have alternatives to procuring been considered and discounted?
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Do you have a budget?
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Is there a robust documented business case supporting this procurement exercise?
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Will this expenditure stand up to public scrutiny?
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Are you aware of opportunities to buy your specific requirement through existing collaborative contracts. If so do you know how to access them?
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholder Map & Degree of Engagement
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: For the procurement exercise to be effective, it must meet the reasonable expectations of stakeholders and end users.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: A clear understanding of stakeholder and end users' views is essential. To obtain this understanding you must have effective stakeholder engagement, taking into account all stakeholder views.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Many stakeholders will be positive and supportive however, it is also important to understand the reasons why stakeholders may not be supportive.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: In order to manage this you may wish to consider some of the following:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Ask your colleagues whether they know of any strong views stakeholders may hold. This will help you gain an understanding of any issues that may arise and reasons for these
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Meet with stakeholders on a 1:1 basis in advance to understand their views and concerns
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Ensure stakeholders are encouraged to contribute fully
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Ensure a good governance structure is in place. This should include identifying and addressing any conflicts of interest
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: The stakeholder map is a useful tool for the UIG to plan communications to stakeholders who are not UIG members.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: You may wish to issue the attached UIG Welcome Pack which covers:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Roles and Responsibilities,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Core competencies,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Business conduct,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Gifts and hospitality and a
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholder Declaration of Interest .
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: A UIG charter should be agreed.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Members of the UIG should not underestimate the amount of time and commitment involved in being a member. Although the UIG may meet only fortnightly or monthly there will be work to be completed in between meetings. Members should come to meetings fully prepared.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: A UIG Membership Template an be used to record UIG membership and contact details. Information can be found in the UIG Information and Templates below.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Stakeholders should:
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: always be open to new ways of shaping the requirement by asking the market and identifying what the market can supply.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: give consideration to the options for shaping the market,
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: encourage the market to develop in such a way that it can meet Organisations’ future requirements.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: assess future demand of the commodity/service. This can be based on team knowledge and expertise, and upon information obtained from non-team members.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Engaging the market provides an opportunity to ensure the services provided are at the forefront of those available. Market sounding should also take into account the knowledge held by others buying Organisations, trade bodies and business support Organisations e.g. Federation of Small Businesses and Chambers of Commerce etc.
heading_path: The UIG will assist you with:

content_blocks.text: Care should be taken to uphold the principles of transparency and equal treatment during such discussions. It is strongly recommended that market sounding activity is documented so that, if challenged, there is a record on file of what took place.
